title: Bribery
takeaway: A country where bribery is normal can never hold its head up.
scene: A short poem about bribery, one of the problems the poet comes back to again and again.

original: جس ملک وچہ رشوت عام ہووے نام اوس دا ذلیل و خوار ہووے
سرخ رو نہ ہوئے جہان اندر جینا اوس لئی سدا دشوار ہووے
transliteration: Jis mulk vich rishvat aam hove, naam os da zaleel-o-khwaar hove
Surkh-roo na hoe jahaan andar, jeena os layi sada dushvaar hove
translation: A country where bribery is common has its name disgraced and humiliated;
it never stands with honour in the world, and life there is always hard.
couplets.story: A country where bribery is normal gets a bad name. It can never stand proudly in the world, and life there stays hard for everyone.

original: پئیا گل وچہ طوق ہے لعنتاں دا ہن پھلن آگے اک ہووے
پاکستان اس لعنت توں پاک ہووے احمدؔ ملک دا بیڑا پار ہووے
transliteration: Paya gal vich tauq hai laanataan da, hun phalan aage ik hove
Pakistan is laanat ton paak hove, Ahmad, mulk da beera paar hove
translation: A collar of curses has been put around its neck; now let it at least stop spreading.
May Pakistan be cleansed of this curse, Ahmad, so the country's boat can reach the shore.
couplets.story: Bribery hangs around the country's neck like a collar of shame. He prays that Pakistan will be free of it, so the country can finally 'reach the shore' and succeed.

deeper: The Prophet said, 'God's curse is on the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes it.' The poet's word 'laanat' (curse) echoes that saying exactly.
why: A clear, short statement about how corruption hurts everyone.
prompt: How does corruption, even small-scale, affect ordinary people?
notes: Line 2 of the second couplet is partly unclear; the general sense is kept.
